questions.key_step: Right triangle CAP gives angle 30 deg, so PAB is equilateral; centroid at distance r.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (angle, equilateral, centroid) with one familiar geometric observation; proof format only. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q2 (L2), a short circle-geometry chain.

questions.key_step: Centroid is circumcentre of an equilateral triangle; write the circle.
questions.justification: One familiar move applied once with tiny numbers.

questions.key_step: OA.OB = 24 (power); AM gives the midpoint circle, HM gives the polar of O.
questions.justification: Three loci in one question; the harmonic-mean locus needs the polar/inversion idea beyond routine practice, and a slip in any part loses the question.

questions.key_step: Director circle radius is sqrt2 times the radius, so radii form a G.P.
questions.justification: Two routine facts chained (director circle, infinite G.P.) and a short computation.

questions.key_step: Radii are the diagonals; tangency gives R-r=10; with R^2+r^2=400 get Rr.
questions.justification: Several routine steps; the only decision is internal tangency, then algebra for the product.

questions.key_step: Parametrise the hypotenuse ends, express the centroid, eliminate theta.
questions.justification: Long parametric elimination with trigonometric bookkeeping and no options to check; a standard locus technique but precision risk.

questions.key_step: Radical axis through the origin and tangency gives ab=0.
questions.justification: Radical axis plus the tangency condition, then a neat factorisation; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Chord of the fixed circle with each member is radical axis; combination of two lines gives the point.
questions.justification: Standard family-of-circles pattern: form the family, subtract, find the fixed point of a pencil.

questions.key_step: Director circle, then point-circle + lambda tangent through (1,1).
questions.justification: Two standard recalls (director circle, family tangent at a point) and one linear equation.

questions.key_step: Fixed points from circle+line pencil; minimal circle has diameter AB.
questions.justification: Pencil of circles and a minimisation; both routine.

questions.key_step: Orthogonality conditions are linear; subtract to get the radical axis.
questions.justification: General proof plus numeric deduction; a known result with routine algebra.

questions.key_step: Centre on the bisector y=x, R=sqrt2 h/3 from the pair of lines, internal tangency fixes h.
questions.justification: Three stages (bisector, tangency to a line pair, internal tangency) with surd-heavy algebra and no options.

questions.key_step: OA = 3/tan(alpha), tan 2alpha = 1/3 solved for tan alpha.
questions.justification: Pair of lines, half-angle and a surd answer; the half-angle quadratic is a mild trap and the answer is unchecked.

questions.key_step: 45 degree line slopes from the tangent slope, then centres along the lines.
questions.justification: Routine slope-angle formula repeated, then points at a given distance; long but no insight.

questions.key_step: Tangents x+y=(2-+sqrt2)r and trapezium area.
questions.justification: Standard tangent-to-axes circle and an area; short routine chain.

questions.key_step: Diameter of C3 is 28 and the internal tangent is perpendicular to the line of centres.
questions.justification: Well-known configuration; Pythagoras once the geometry is set up.

questions.key_step: Centres on the bisector, h = r cot(theta/2); product of roots of a quadratic in r.
questions.justification: Needs the idea that the two circles are the two roots of one quadratic; three stages with trigonometric half-angle.

questions.key_step: Tangency of the slanted side to the incircle gives r = ab/(a+b).
questions.justification: Coordinate set-up and a distance condition; a familiar result with routine algebra.

questions.key_step: All vertices on the big circle, so tangent lengths are equal and the triangle is equilateral.
questions.justification: Proof needs the insight that equal tangent lengths force an equilateral triangle, then inradius = R/2.

questions.key_step: Radical axis, then half-chord and a difference of squares.
questions.justification: Routine algebra; the factorisation is the only care point.

questions.key_step: Upper semicircle and a line crossing the diameter inside the circle.
questions.justification: One counting observation from a simple picture.

questions.key_step: Ends of a diameter on y=1 and Thales (or expand and use the circle equation).
questions.justification: Two short steps with a small insight (angle in a semicircle).

questions.key_step: Director circle has radius r sqrt2, annulus area pi r^2.
questions.justification: One standard fact applied once.

questions.key_step: Radius CQ is at angle pi/2 - theta, so Q = C + (sin, cos).
questions.justification: Setting up the angle from the figure; short but a sign slip is possible.

questions.key_step: Tangent at Q is perpendicular to CQ; simplify with sin^2+cos^2=1.
questions.justification: Routine tangent line with trigonometric simplification.

questions.key_step: Area = kite - sector with central angle pi-theta.
questions.justification: Needs the kite-minus-sector construction and half-angle value of cot(pi/8); precision risk.

questions.key_step: Centre distance sqrt2(b-a) turns each condition into a quadratic in b/a.
questions.justification: Four separate derivations including the longest-common-chord condition (C2 bisects C1); each is short but the set is long, so above 2024-P1-Q15 (L1).
